Microplastic transport in tidal estuaries: a field and modelling study

Highlights

  • Microplastics were sampled at 24 stations across three estuaries over a full year.
  • Tidal pumping retained up to 60% of particles inside the estuary.
  • A particle-tracking model reproduced field concentrations within 20%.

Graphical abstract

Graphical summary of sampling sites and modelled particle pathways across the three estuaries studied.

Abstract

Estuaries are thought to be major pathways for microplastics from land to sea, yet how tides control their export is poorly known. We combined a year of field sampling at 24 stations with a three-dimensional particle-tracking model. Tidal pumping retained most particles inside the estuaries, and only storm events produced net export to the coastal ocean.

Keywords

Microplastics

1. Introduction

Plastic pollution is everywhere. Rivers carry particles to estuaries where tides mix them.

4. Discussion

4.1. Retention

Retention dominated in all seasons except winter storms.

5. Conclusions

Tidal estuaries act as filters that retain most microplastics, releasing them mainly during storms.
Monitoring programmes should therefore sample during storm events to capture the bulk of the export.
